Let \(A=k[a,b,c,d]\). The relations say that \(R\) is generated from \(A\) by two commuting skew variables:
\[
x f=\sigma(f)x,\qquad y f=\tau(f)y\qquad (f\in A),
\]
where
\[
\sigma(a,b,c,d)=(-a,-b-a,-c-2b-a,-d-3c-3b-a)
\]
and
\[
\tau(a,b,c,d)=(-a,a-b,-c+2b-a,-d+3c-3b+a).
\]
Write \(T=\exp D\), where
\[
D=a\frac{\partial}{\partial b}+2b\frac{\partial}{\partial c}+3c\frac{\partial}{\partial d}.
\]
Then
\[
\sigma=-T,\qquad \tau=-T^{-1},
\]
so \(\tau=\sigma^{-1}\). Hence
\[
x^m y^n f=\sigma^{m-n}(f)x^m y^n.
\]
Since \(\sigma\) has infinite order in characteristic \(0\), a monomial \(x^m y^n\) can commute with all of \(A\) only when \(m=n\). Thus every central element is a polynomial in \(xy\) with coefficients in \(A^\sigma\):
\[
Z(R)=A^\sigma[xy].
\]

It remains to compute \(A^\sigma\). Since \(\sigma^2=T^2=\exp(2D)\), any \(\sigma\)-fixed element lies in \(\ker D\). Conversely, on \(\ker D\), the action of \(\sigma\) is just simultaneous sign change
\[
(a,b,c,d)\mapsto(-a,-b,-c,-d),
\]
so \(A^\sigma\) is the even-degree part of \(\ker D\).

A standard slice computation for
\[
D=a\partial_b+2b\partial_c+3c\partial_d
\]
gives
\[
\ker D
=
k[a,u,v,w],
\]
with one relation, where
\[
u=ac-b^2,
\]
\[
v=a^2d-3abc+2b^3,
\]
\[
w=a^2d^2-6abcd+4b^3d-3b^2c^2+4ac^3,
\]
and
\[
v^2+4u^3=a^2w.
\]
Here \(a,u,v,w\) have total degrees \(1,2,3,4\). Therefore the even part is generated by
\[
a^2,\qquad u,\qquad av,\qquad w.
\]

So the center is
\[
\boxed{
Z(R)=
k\!\left[
xy,\,
a^2,\,
ac-b^2,\,
a(a^2d-3abc+2b^3),\,
a^2d^2-6abcd+4b^3d-3b^2c^2+4ac^3
\right].
}
\]

Equivalently, if
\[
U=ac-b^2,\quad
V=a(a^2d-3abc+2b^3),\quad
W=a^2d^2-6abcd+4b^3d-3b^2c^2+4ac^3,
\]
then
\[
Z(R)=k[xy,a^2,U,V,W],
\]
with the internal relation
\[
V^2=a^2\bigl(a^2W-4U^3\bigr).
\]
